question.text: Will the operating rooms of Hospital Privado de Mendoza be open for new surgeries on November 13, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, as of the end of November 13, 2026 (Mendoza local time, UTC−3), the preventive suspension of surgical activity at the Hospital Privado de Mendoza ordered by the provincial health ministry in October 2026 has been lifted such that the hospital is again authorised to perform new scheduled (non-emergency) operations — including where the lifting is partial or phased, provided at least one of the hospital's operating rooms may again carry out new scheduled surgeries. It resolves NO if the suspension remains fully in force on that date, if only emergency or urgent operations are permitted, or if no credible report indicates any resumption of scheduled surgery at the hospital by then. Resolution is based on announcements from the [Ministerio de Salud y Deportes de Mendoza](https://www.mendoza.gov.ar/salud/), statements by the hospital, or reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions); where reports conflict, provincial health ministry statements govern.
question.fine_print: Evidence that new scheduled operations have in fact been performed at the hospital after the suspension was lifted also counts, even if the ministry issued no formal announcement. The question concerns only the Hospital Privado de Mendoza at Av. Bartolomé Mitre 653, Mendoza city, Argentina.

research:
I found nothing showing that scheduled surgery has resumed or that the suspension has been lifted. The latest report, Los Andes on 3 Nov, still describes surgical activity as preventively suspended, and no reopening date has been announced.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: I read the ministry's health page (it redirects to mendoza.gob.ar/saludydeportes). It has no item mentioning meningitis, the Hospital Privado, operating rooms or Serratia. I found no data file, dashboard or press release about lifting the suspension. [ministry](https://www.mendoza.gob.ar/saludydeportes/)
- I could not find any hospital statement about resuming surgery.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. Every source I found, the newest dated 3 Nov, says surgical activity at the hospital is still preventively suspended.
- 2026-11-03: Los Andes says the ministry "suspendió preventivamente la actividad quirúrgica". It also reports:
  - Bacterial isolates were sent to the national reference lab, Instituto Malbrán, to test whether the cases are linked.
  - No contamination source has been officially confirmed.
  - A patient's family has filed a criminal complaint, and prosecutors have asked for his medical records.
  - [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Case story about Carlos Bordón, operated on 14 Oct, now in intensive care with Serratia meningitis. The criminal complaint is with the Unidad Fiscal Correccional. Malbrán genotyping results are still pending. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)
- 2026-10-29: The operating rooms remain "cerrados preventivamente". Two more deaths are under investigation within a group of 10 patients. No common source has been found yet. Epidemiology director Andrea Falaschi says investigators are also looking at the building, how people enter the operating rooms, and patient preparation protocols. No reopening date. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/29/brote-de-meningitis-en-mendoza-investigan-dos-fallecimientos-mas-en-el-hospital-privado/); [La Arena](http://www.laarena.com.ar/la-region/brote-de-meningitis-investigan-dos-fallecimientos-mas-2026102911500)
- 2026-10-27: 5 confirmed cases, 3 suspected and 2 ruled out, with samples going to Malbrán for genotyping. [Sitio Andino](https://www.sitioandino.com.ar/salud/brote-meningitis-mendoza-se-confirmo-un-nuevo-caso-y-son-diez-los-pacientes-investigados-n5732665); [MDZ](https://www.mdzol.com/sociedad/2026/10/27/confirmaron-un-nuevo-caso-de-meningitis-que-se-sabe-y-como-estan-los-pacientes-1991085.html)
- 2026-10-26: Falaschi said the operating rooms must undergo several improvements before they can work again. Neither the improvements nor a timeline were specified. [Memo](https://www.memo.com.ar/economia/meningitis-en-el-hospital-privado-salud-investiga-el-origen-del-brote-y-no-descarta-una-contaminacion-en-el-quirofano); [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/mendoza-en-alerta-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-en-un-hospital-dos-los-cuatro-contagiados-fallecieron-nid26102026/)
- 2026-10-24: Besides the operating rooms, the hospital pharmacy was closed. Antiseptics, anesthetics, medications, solutions and surgical instruments were seized for testing. Surgery stays suspended until lab results are evaluated and conditions for reopening are set. The hospital says it had stopped surgeries itself on Tuesday 20 Oct, before the ministry stepped in. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/24/mendoza-cerro-los-quirofanos-de-un-hospital-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-posquirurgica-murieron-dos-pacientes/); [El Sol](https://www.elsol.com.ar/mendoza/suspendieron-las-cirugias-en-el-hospital-privado-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-posquirurgica/); [Pasa en MDZ](https://pasaenmdz.com/brote-de-meningitis-en-el-hospital-privado-suspenden-cirugias-tras-la-muerte-de-dos-pacientes-y-fallas-en-el-control-sanitario/)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic data on how long operating rooms stay shut after a deadly infection outbreak. The comparable cases I found:
  - **Durango, Mexico, 2022-23:** a meningitis outbreak was traced to contaminated anesthesia, and the private hospitals involved had their operating rooms closed. The clinics never reopened normally, and in May 2026 the owners were sentenced to 24 years in prison. That outbreak was far larger (dozens of deaths). [El Imparcial](https://www.elimparcial.com/mexico/2026/05/15/propietarios-de-hospital-en-durango-son-sentenciados-a-24-anos-de-prision-por-su-responsabilidad-en-el-brote-de-meningitis-aseptica-asociado-a-anestesia-contaminada-que-dejo-41-personas-fallecidas-entre-2022-y-2023/); [UnoTV](https://www.unotv.com/estados/durango/meningitis-aseptica-en-durango-por-casos-suspenden-cirugias-en-hospitales-privados/)
  - **Lleida, Spain:** Arnau de Vilanova hospital closed six operating rooms on 23 Oct 2026 after a water leak. They were due to reopen on 3 Nov (about 11 days), once cleaning was done and microbiological cultures came back negative. No one died there, so it is the easier case. [El Periódico](https://www.elperiodico.com/es/sanidad/20261102/hospital-arnau-reabre-quirofanos-136008354)
- By 13 Nov the Mendoza suspension will have lasted 22 to 24 days. Lifting it seems to depend on three things: Malbrán results, identifying the source, and the improvements Falaschi mentioned.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction-market prices supplied match this question. They cover hotel room counts, embassy reopening, a Mendoza football match, Fernando Mendoza's NFL debut and Arizona's 6th district. I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market or expert forecast on this hospital.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Malbrán genotyping results, which could identify a common source such as a contaminated anesthetic or solution. No date has been given.
- Results on the seized supplies and the environmental samples.
- The ministry's verdict on the required operating-room improvements and any re-inspection.
- Whether the two extra deaths under investigation are linked to the outbreak, and whether new cases appear.
- The criminal case with the Unidad Fiscal Correccional, which could add legal hurdles to reopening.
- A partial or phased reopening of even one operating room for scheduled surgery would be enough for YES.

## Hospital Privado de Mendoza surgical suspension: research summary (as of 2026-11-03)

As of 3 November I found nothing showing the suspension has been lifted. No reopening date, timetable or set of reopening criteria has been published. The investigation is still open: Malbrán genotyping results are pending and a criminal inquiry is under way.

### 1. Resolution source
- **Ministry press site:** I searched the ministry's press site for "meningitis" and got one release: "El Ministerio de Salud dispuso el cierre preventivo de quirófanos de un hospital privado ante un brote de meningitis posquirúrgica". It reports four Serratia marcescens infections and two deaths, and says preventive measures stay in place. I found no later release about reopening. [prensa.mendoza.gob.ar](https://prensa.mendoza.gob.ar/?s=meningitis)
- **The hospital:** I found no public statement from the Hospital Privado on reopening.

### 2. Current status
- **2026-11-03:** Los Andes says surgery is still suspended as a preventive measure and gives no reopening date. Samples and isolates went to the Instituto Malbrán, a national reference laboratory, to check whether the bacteria from different patients are related. There is still no official finding on how the contagion happened. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)
- **Bottom line:** Nothing settles the question yet. The suspension is fully in force as far as reporting shows, and the stated condition for lifting it is that the investigation concludes and the hospital makes improvements.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- **2026-11-03:** Los Andes profiles Carlos Bordón, 59, who had hip surgery on 14 Oct. He deteriorated on 16 Oct and now has Serratia meningitis at Hospital Central. His daughters filed a criminal complaint and the hospital's clinical records were requested. A related headline on the page cites 5 confirmed infections and 4 deaths under study, out of 10 patients investigated. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-el-hospital-privado-un-hombre-entro-operarse-la-cadera-y-lucha-su-vida-n6012696)
- **2026-10-29:** Infobae reports the operating rooms are "cerrados preventivamente" and two more deaths are under investigation. Falaschi said investigators are looking at anesthesia, infusions, surgical materials, the building, operating room access routes and patient-preparation protocols. No reopening criteria or date were given. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/29/brote-de-meningitis-en-mendoza-investigan-dos-fallecimientos-mas-en-el-hospital-privado/)
- **2026-10-28:** La Nación: "crece la incertidumbre sobre el origen" and two possible new cases are being analysed. [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/brote-de-meningitis-en-mendoza-crece-la-incertidumbre-sobre-el-origen-y-analizan-nuevos-casos-nid28102026/)
- **2026-10-27:** Diario Uno counts 5 confirmed cases, 3 suspected and 2 ruled out. One confirmed case is a surgical-site infection from a September operation, so the exposure window may be longer. Falaschi: "Por ahora, el quirófano sigue cerrado". The hospital has to make improvements before it can resume. [Diario Uno](https://www.diariouno.com.ar/sociedad/meningitis-posquirurgica-confirmaron-el-quinto-contagio-y-son-10-los-casos-que-se-investigan-n1610487)
- **2026-10-26:** A criminal complaint is on file with the Unidad Fiscal Correccional (case P-114310/26). Prosecutors are examining "propagación culposa o dolosa". [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/sociedad/cual-es-la-investigacion-que-sigue-la-justicia-el-brote-meningitis-un-hospital-mendoza-n6011783), [MDZ](https://www.mdzol.com/sociedad/2026/10/26/meningitis-en-mendoza-la-justicia-ya-investiga-el-brote-en-el-hospital-privado-1990859.html)
- **2026-10-26:** The ministry says results from ten samples will be released only once they are final. Sitio Andino also reports public anger over the outbreak. [Sitio Andino](https://www.sitioandino.com.ar/salud/tras-el-brote-meningitis-y-las-muertes-el-hospital-privado-estallo-la-indignacion-social-n5732621)
- **2026-10-24:** Infobae reports that the hospital's pharmacy was also shut, and that antiseptics, anesthetics and instruments were seized. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/sociedad/2026/10/24/mendoza-cerro-los-quirofanos-de-un-hospital-por-un-brote-de-meningitis-posquirurgica-murieron-dos-pacientes/)

### 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic base rate for how long operating rooms stay shut after a deadly hospital outbreak in Argentina.
- **Closest analogue:** In Durango, Mexico (2022-23), meningitis after spinal anesthesia led to operating room closures at private hospitals that lasted months. [Vanguardia](https://vanguardia.com.mx/noticias/24-mujeres-tienen-meningitis-en-durango-clausuran-quirofanos-de-hospital-privado-YF5007616)
- **Much less severe case:** In Lleida, Spain, six operating rooms shut by a water leak on 23 Oct 2026 reopened on 3 Nov after disinfection and negative cultures, about 11 days later. That case had no deaths and no criminal inquiry (news API item, El Periódico).
- **Timing:** 13 November will be 22 days after the 22 October closure. Here the source is still unknown, Malbrán genotyping is pending, there are possibly 4 deaths and the exposure window may reach back to September. All of that points to a longer closure than in a simple decontamination case. This is my reading of the context, not a forecast.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction-market prices supplied match this question. The "Mendoza" markets are about football, an NFL player and an Arizona election, and the others are about hotels and the US government.
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus forecast on this hospital.

### 6. Upcoming events that could move the outcome
- Malbrán genotyping results (no date given).
- The ministry releasing final results on the ten samples.
- Whether the two extra deaths are confirmed or ruled out.
- Any newly reported cases, which would probably prolong the closure.
- The ministry checking the improvements the hospital is required to make.
- Possible pressure from PAMI to reopen, since many retiree surgeries are backlogged. I found no reporting on this.
- Prosecutors' steps in case P-114310/26.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain until the end of 13 November 2026 (Mendoza time). For YES, the provincial ministry must lift the October suspension, fully or partially, so that at least one operating room may again perform new scheduled (non-emergency) surgery. Alternatively, there must be credible evidence that such surgeries have actually resumed.

(b) Status quo: the operating rooms and the pharmacy remain preventively closed. As of 3 November there is no reopening date, no confirmed source of contamination, and Malbrán genotyping is still pending. If nothing changes, the question resolves NO.

(c) Base rate: there is little systematic data. For operating rooms closed by health authorities after a fatal surgical-site or meningitis outbreak, reopening within about 3 weeks looks uncommon. Two rough reference points:
- Closures for non-fatal environmental problems, such as the Lleida water leak, often reopen in 10 to 14 days.
- Fatal outbreaks with an unidentified source, deaths and litigation usually take a month or more, and Durango never reopened normally.

A blended base rate for reopening by day 22 to 24 is roughly 20 to 30%.

(d) Evidence:
- For YES:
  - The leading hypothesis is a single contaminated item, such as an antiseptic, anesthetic or solution. If that is confirmed, the fix is removing the item plus disinfection, which can be fast.
  - The hospital is a PAMI provider with strong economic and patient-access pressure to resume.
  - On 26 October the outbreak was reported as not spreading further.
  - On 26 October Falaschi framed reopening as conditional on "improvements", which implies a defined path to reopening.
- For NO:
  - As of 3 November (Los Andes) the source was still not confirmed and Malbrán results were pending.
  - On 29 October two further deaths were under investigation, and investigators had widened their scope to the building, operating-room access and patient-preparation protocols.
  - A criminal complaint has been filed and prosecutors have requested medical records.
  - There is national media attention and up to 4 deaths, so the ministry is politically sensitive about reopening.
  - No timetable has been announced.

(e) Scenarios:
- NO: Malbrán results arrive in mid-November or later, the ministry requires structural and protocol improvements and then a re-inspection, and the closure stretches into late November or December.
- YES: Malbrán quickly links the cases to a specific contaminated lot. The hospital completes disinfection, discards the lot and submits new protocols. The ministry then authorises a phased reopening of one operating room around 10 to 13 November, and local media report it.

(f) I start from about 25%. Three factors pull the estimate down:
- The source is still unconfirmed with lab results pending.
- The investigation has broadened rather than narrowed.
- The fatalities, criminal case and media attention make the ministry cautious.

Two factors partly offset this: the hospital's economic pressure and the possibility of a quick single-item explanation. There is also a small risk that a quiet partial reopening goes unreported. Overall I move slightly down from the base rate.

Probability: 20%

**(a) Time left and what is needed for Yes.** About 10 days remain, until the end of 13 Nov 2026 (Mendoza time). Yes requires one of two things before then:
- the Mendoza health ministry lifts the preventive suspension, fully or partially, so that at least one operating room may again do new scheduled surgeries, or
- credible reports show scheduled operations have actually resumed.

Permission for emergency surgery only does not count.

**(b) Status quo.** The suspension is fully in force as of 3 Nov. No source of contamination has been identified, Malbrán genotyping is pending, and no reopening date exists. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

**(c) Base rate.** I found no clean data on how long operating rooms stay shut after a deadly outbreak, so this rests on judgement from a few cases:
- Closures without deaths, such as the Lleida water leak, last about 1 to 2 weeks.
- Fatal outbreaks under active investigation, with lab confirmation from a national reference lab and a criminal complaint, usually keep rooms closed for several weeks to months.
- Durango never reopened normally.

For fatal outbreaks of this type, reopening within about 3 weeks probably happens around 20-30% of the time.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - The hospital is a private PAMI provider, so there is strong economic and patient-access pressure to restart surgery.
  - The leading hypothesis (26 Oct) is a contaminated supply item. If a specific batch of solution or anesthetic is confirmed, replacing it, disinfecting and running negative cultures could allow a fast phased reopening.
  - The case count had not grown much as of 26 to 29 Oct.
- For No:
  - On 26 Oct, epidemiology director Falaschi said the rooms cannot function until a series of improvements is made.
  - On 29 Oct, two more deaths were under investigation, and investigators had widened their scope to the building, operating-room access and patient preparation protocols.
  - On 3 Nov, Los Andes reported surgery still suspended, no confirmed source and Malbrán results pending.
  - A criminal complaint has been filed and prosecutors have requested records.
  - The pharmacy was closed and supplies were seized.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: Malbrán results arrive in mid-November or later, the ministry requires infrastructure and protocol changes plus a re-inspection, and with up to four deaths and media scrutiny, officials avoid any quick reopening. The suspension continues past 13 Nov.
- Yes: Around 5 to 10 Nov, lab tests trace Serratia to a specific contaminated antiseptic or solution lot. The hospital discards it, cleans the rooms, environmental cultures come back negative, and the ministry authorizes a phased reopening of one or two rooms by about 12 Nov.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** I start at about 25%. As of 3 Nov there is no confirmed source, required improvements are still unspecified, and a criminal case and investigations into additional deaths are adding caution, so I move down slightly. The economic pressure from PAMI and the possibility of a single-lot explanation keep the probability meaningfully above zero.

Probability: 20%

(a) About 10 days remain, until the end of November 13, 2026 (Mendoza time). For YES, the provincial ministry must lift or partially lift the preventive suspension so that at least one operating room may again perform new scheduled (non-emergency) surgery, or credible reports must show such surgeries actually resumed.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is NO. As of the latest report (Los Andes, Nov 3), the operating rooms remain preventively closed, with no reopening date or criteria announced.

(c) Base rate: there is no systematic data, so I used a rough reference class.
- When a hospital's operating rooms are closed after a fatal outbreak that is still unresolved, they often stay closed for several weeks to months.
- Closures for simpler environmental problems (like the Lleida water leak) resolve in about 1 to 2 weeks.
- Fatal outbreaks under active investigation, especially with criminal complaints, tend to run longer. Durango is the extreme case, where the clinics never reopened normally.
- A suspension of about 3 weeks ending within that window in an unresolved fatal case happens perhaps 25 to 35% of the time.

(d) Evidence for each side:
- **For YES:**
  - The leading hypothesis (Oct 26) is a contaminated supply item. Supplies were seized and the pharmacy closed. If a contaminated lot is identified and removed, the rooms could reopen after disinfection and negative cultures.
  - The hospital has strong economic pressure to resume, as a PAMI provider with mainly pensioner surgical patients.
  - A partial or phased reopening counts toward YES.
- **For NO:**
  - No source was confirmed as of Nov 3.
  - Malbrán genotyping is still pending.
  - Falaschi (Oct 26) said a series of improvements must be completed before the rooms can function again.
  - On Oct 29, investigators widened their scope to the building, access to the operating rooms and patient preparation protocols.
  - Two more deaths are under investigation.
  - A criminal complaint is now with prosecutors.
  - There are up to 4 deaths, so the ministry faces political pressure to be cautious.

(e) Scenarios:
- **NO:** Malbrán results arrive mid-November or later, or are inconclusive. The ministry requires infrastructure and protocol changes plus a re-inspection, so the suspension continues past Nov 13, perhaps with only emergency procedures allowed.
- **YES:** Testing in early November identifies a contaminated antiseptic or solution lot. The hospital replaces its supplies, completes the required improvements, passes environmental cultures and a re-inspection, and the ministry authorizes a phased restart of scheduled surgery around Nov 10 to 13.

(f) I start at about 30% from the reference class. I move down slightly because no source has been confirmed this late, the scope of the investigation is widening, the criminal case is new, and there was no sign of a reopening plan in the Nov 3 reporting. The partial-reopening clause and the economic pressure on the hospital stop me from going much lower.

Probability: 22%

(a) About 10 days remain, until the end of 13 November 2026 (Mendoza time). For Yes, the provincial ministry must lift the preventive suspension, at least partially, so that the hospital can again perform new scheduled (non-emergency) surgeries. Credible evidence that scheduled operations have resumed would also count.

(b) The status quo is No. As of 3 November the operating rooms remain fully closed. No reopening date or criteria have been given, and lifting the closure depends on the investigation concluding and the hospital making the required improvements.

(c) Base rate: closures of operating rooms after deadly post-surgical infection outbreaks with an unresolved source tend to last weeks to months. The Durango meningitis closures lasted months. Simple contamination events with no deaths, such as the Lleida water leak, reopen in about 10 to 14 days. Weighting toward the severe end of that range, the share of comparable deadly, unresolved outbreaks that reopened within 22 days is roughly 20 to 30%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The leading hypothesis is a contaminated item (26 October), which could allow reopening once supplies are replaced, the rooms are disinfected and cultures come back negative.
  - The private hospital and PAMI's backlog of retiree surgeries create economic pressure to reopen.
  - Falaschi said the outbreak had not spread further for the time being (26 October).
- **For No:**
  - Confirmed cases have grown to 5, with up to 4 deaths under study (27 October to 3 November).
  - The exposure window may extend back to September.
  - Malbrán genotyping is still pending, and the source was officially unknown as of 3 November.
  - A criminal case is open (P-114310/26), the pharmacy was also closed and supplies were seized.
